========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well... I guess I’m here because I just... I don't care about anything anymore. And I mean literally anything. It’s like someone just reached into my head and unplugged the part of me that actually wants to do things or be alive. I used to be so active, you know? I was taking these art classes at the community college—watercolor and acrylics mostly, I was actually getting really good at painting landscapes and mixing colors—but now my supplies are just sitting in the corner collecting dust and I can't even bring myself to look at them. 

And it’s not just the art. I used to host these big board-game nights every other Thursday with my friends, we’d play Settlers of Catan or those really long strategy games for hours, but I haven't answered their texts in weeks. I just don't see the point. Same with hiking. I used to go out on the trails every single weekend, rain or shine, just to be outside. I was even talking about getting back on my old recreational soccer team, the one I played with a few years ago, because I missed running around... but now? Now I just sit in my room. All day. I just sit there on the edge of my bed, staring at the wall or the floor, and I watch the hours go by. I just let everything slip away. It's like I'm watching my whole life disappear from the inside of my bedroom, all the things that used to make me *me*, and I don't even have the energy to care that it's happening. I don't know how it got this bad, I really don't, but I just can't make myself care about a single thing.

Well... it's been a really long time. I mean, I remember it starting to get bad, like really bad, around the summer of last year. So, I guess that makes it... what, a year and four months? Yeah, about a year and four months where it's just been this constant, heavy blanket over everything. But honestly, it feels like it's been a lifetime.

I had signed up for this advanced watercolor technique course at the community college—it was on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and the instructor was this amazing local artist who I'd been wanting to learn from for years. July hit, and it was just like someone flipped a switch. I never went to a single class. I couldn't even make myself drive to the campus. I just sat in my room with the AC running, staring at the blank paper, feeling absolutely nothing.

I usually do the Ridge Trail in October because the colors are incredible. But I didn't go once. Then winter, then spring, and now here we are again, and it's just been this endless stretch of... nothing. Sixteen months of just sitting on the edge of my bed, watching the seasons change outside my window and not caring at all. Sixteen months of ignoring texts from my board-game friends. I... yeah. I have. I mean, it's not like I have this detailed plan with a date circled on a calendar or anything, but... the thoughts are just there. All the time. It's like this constant background noise in my head, just whispering that it would be so much easier if I just... wasn't here anymore. I don't want to open my eyes and face another day of this heavy, suffocating nothingness. It's exhausting. It's just so physically and mentally exhausting to exist like this.

And... well, it actually got really scary a couple of weeks ago. My friend Sarah, she's the one who used to organize the board game nights, she actually came over because I hadn't answered her texts in weeks. She used her spare key—I gave it to her years ago to feed my cat when I went on a hiking trip, back when I actually did things—and she found me just sitting on the floor in the hallway. I hadn't moved in hours. And... she said I was just rocking back and forth, and I was saying it out loud. Over and over. I was just repeating, "I can't keep living like this, I can't keep living like this." I didn't even realize I was saying it until she grabbed my shoulders and shook me. It just... it spilled out of me because it's true. I really don't think I can keep living like this. It hurts too much, even though it's just emptiness, it somehow hurts so much, and I just want it to stop. I just want to go to sleep and never, ever have to wake up and feel this way again.

Well... yeah. Yes, I do. It's... it's really hard to talk about because I know how it sounds, you know? I know it sounds crazy, but it's so real to me. It's... it's a woman's voice. It's gotten to the point where I'm scared to even look in that corner of the room, even during the day, because I just know she's there, waiting to start again. It's like I'm trapped behind this thick glass wall, and even when I try to reach out and explain what's happening to me, it just comes out as a tangled mess of random words. It just makes me not want to try talking at all, because what's the point if no one can follow my thoughts anyway?

Yeah, exactly. That's exactly what I was just trying to explain. It happens all the time, just like I was saying. But honestly, it feels like it's been a lifetime. \n\nI remember last summer so clearly because that was supposed to be when I finally went back to my art classes. I had signed up for this advanced watercolor technique course at the community college—it was on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, and the instructor was this amazing local artist who I'd been wanting to learn from for years. I had even bought this special cold-pressed paper, the really expensive kind that doesn't warp when it gets wet, and I was so ready. But then... July hit, and it was just like someone flipped a switch. I never went to a single class. I couldn't even make myself drive to the campus. I just sat in my room with the AC running, staring at the blank paper, feeling absolutely nothing. \n\nAnd it hasn't let up since. Not for a single day. Fall came, and usually I love the fall—the leaves changing, the crisp air, that's prime hiking season for me. I usually do the Ridge Trail in October because the colors are incredible. But I didn't go once. Then winter, then spring, and now here we are again, and it's just been this endless stretch of... nothing. Sixteen months of just sitting on the edge of my bed, watching the seasons change outside my window and not caring at all. Sixteen months of ignoring texts from my board-game friends. I mean, they don't even text me anymore, really. Why would they? I haven't been a person for a year and four months. It's just been this constant, unrelenting emptiness since last summer, every single day, from the minute I wake up until I finally manage to fall asleep.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever think that things will never get better for you?\n\nPatient: Well... yeah. Honestly, yeah, all the time. It's just... it's like this constant, suffocating weight, you know? Most days, almost every single day, I wake up and before I even open my eyes, I can feel it. It's this heavy, hollow feeling right here in the center of my chest, like someone scooped out everything that makes a person human and just poured lead in there instead. And when I finally do open my eyes and look around my room—at the dust on my easel, at the hiking boots I haven't touched in over a year—it just hits me that this is it. This is all there is. \n\nI just lie there and think, \"What's the point of even getting up?\" Because I look ahead, into tomorrow, or next week, or next year, and I don't see anything. I don't see myself painting again, I don't see myself laughing at a board game, I don't see myself running on a soccer field. I just see these four walls. It feels like there is absolutely no future for me beyond the walls of this apartment. Like my whole life has already happened, and now I'm just... existing in the aftermath of it. I try to remember what it felt like to have hope, to look forward to something, like how I used to look forward to that Tuesday night watercolor class, but I can't even grasp the concept of it anymore. It's just this endless, gray tunnel, and I'm stuck right in the middle of it, and I really, truly believe that this is just how it's going to be forever. I don't see how it could possibly ever get better when it's been this dark for so long.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever thought about harming yourself or wished you were dead?\n\nPatient: I... yeah. I have. I mean, it's not like I have this detailed plan with a date circled on a calendar or anything, but... the thoughts are just there. All the time. It's like this constant background noise in my head, just whispering that it would be so much easier if I just... wasn't here anymore. Every night when I finally manage to fall asleep, which is a whole struggle on its own, my last thought before I drift off is always, \"I hope I don't wake up tomorrow.\" I just don't want to wake up. I don't want to open my eyes and face another day of this heavy, suffocating nothingness. It's exhausting. It's just so physically and mentally exhausting to exist like this.\n\nAnd... well, it actually got really scary a couple of weeks ago. My friend Sarah, she's the one who used to organize the board game nights, she actually came over because I hadn't answered her texts in weeks. She used her spare key—I gave it to her years ago to feed my cat when I went on a hiking trip, back when I actually did things—and she found me just sitting on the floor in the hallway. I hadn't moved in hours. And... she said I was just rocking back and forth, and I was saying it out loud. Over and over. I was just repeating, \"I can't keep living like this, I can't keep living like this.\" I didn't even realize I was saying it until she grabbed my shoulders and shook me. It just... it spilled out of me because it's true. I really don't think I can keep living like this. It hurts too much, even though it's just emptiness, it somehow hurts so much, and I just want it to stop. I just want to go to sleep and never, ever have to wake up and feel this way again.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices or seen things that aren't there when you're alone?\n\nPatient: Well... yeah. Yes, I do. It's... it's really hard to talk about because I know how it sounds, you know? I know it sounds crazy, but it's so real to me. It's... it's a woman's voice. And it always comes from the exact same spot, right in the corner of my bedroom, near where the window meets the closet. I'll just be lying there in bed, staring at the ceiling, feeling that heavy emptiness I was telling you about, and then... she'll just start talking. \n\nIt's not like a thought in my head, it's not like my internal monologue. She just lists all my failures, over and over, and she tells me that I need to stay inside. I've tried putting in headphones, turning the AC up louder, burying my head under the pillows, but she just cuts right through all of it. Sometimes she talks for just a few minutes, but other times it feels like she goes on for hours, just this relentless, clear voice coming from the shadows in the corner, telling me how useless I am and how I have to stay hidden away. It's gotten to the point where I'm scared to even look in that corner of the room, even during the day, because I just know she's there, waiting to start again. It makes the emptiness feel so much worse, because even when I'm completely alone and isolated, I'm still being punished, you know? It's just... it's so loud, and I can't escape it.\n\nDoctor: Does the voice you hear ever tell you to do things, or is it only criticizing you?\n\nPatient: Well... she mostly just criticizes me, like I said. It's... it's not like she's giving me commands to, you know, go out and do something specific, or... or hurt someone, or anything like that. It's more like she's just dictating my reality, if that makes sense? Like, she's not saying, \"Go lock the door,\" she's saying, \"You ruined everything, you have to stay inside.\" \n\nAnd it's just... it's so specific to that one spot. She tells me how I've completely destroyed my life, how I've ruined every good thing I ever had. And she tells me I need to stay inside. She says it over and over, that I should stay inside, that I belong in this room, hidden away because I'm such a disaster. \n\nAnd I know I already told you this, but I just... It sounds as clear... as absolutely, undeniably clear as someone standing right next to my bed. Like if you were standing there right now, talking to me, that's exactly what it sounds like. It has volume, it has tone, it has... presence. It fills the room. Even when I try to block it out, even when I pull the blankets over my ears or try to hum to myself, she's just right there, telling me I ruined everything and that I can never leave that room. It's just... it's so exhausting to be trapped with her.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever find it hard to follow your own thoughts or to express them in a way that makes sense to others?\n\nPatient: Yeah... yes, actually. It's... it's really frustrating. It's like my brain is a radio scanning through stations way too fast, and I can't get it to stop on just one. Like, I'll be trying to explain to someone—maybe Sarah, or even just trying to write down what's been happening to me—and I'll start off making sense, I think. I'll start talking about... well, the divorce papers. They've just been sitting there on the kitchen island for I don't even know how long, just this thick stack of heavy, official paper that I can't bring myself to deal with. \n\nAnd then, while I'm trying to talk about the papers and how heavy they feel, I'll notice the color of them, this stark, blinding white, and suddenly my brain just completely shifts to paint colors. Because I used to paint, you know, with the watercolors before I stopped going to the class, and I'll start talking about titanium white and how it mixes with ultramarine, and how the colors just bleed into the texture of the canvas... and then, before I even realize I've changed the subject again, I'm suddenly obsessing over the number seven. I don't even know why it's seven, maybe it's because there were seven pages in the first section of the legal packet, or... or just the sharp shape of the number itself, but I'll just start talking about seven and how important it is. \n\nAnd it feels connected in my head! It feels like it all makes perfect, logical sense in that exact split second. But then I look at whoever I'm talking to, and they just have this blank, worried look on their face. Sarah does it a lot. She'll just gently put her hand on my arm, or she'll kind of interrupt me, and people keep telling me that they can't follow what I'm saying. They say, \"I'm sorry, I lost you, what does the number seven have to do with the divorce papers or the paint?\" And I can't explain it to them because by the time they ask, the connection is gone, the thought has vanished, and I'm just left feeling stupid and even more isolated. It's like I'm trapped behind this thick glass wall, and even when I try to reach out and explain what's happening to me, it just comes out as a tangled mess of random words. It just makes me not want to try talking at all, because what's the point if no one can follow my thoughts anyway?\n\nDoctor: Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking or thinking?\n\nPatient: Yeah, exactly. That's exactly what I was just trying to explain. It happens all the time, just like I was saying. I go straight from the stark white of those legal documents to the titanium white paint colors I used to use, thinking about how I used to mix it with just a tiny drop of ultramarine to make the perfect sky color for these landscapes I used to do before everything got so dark. And then, before I can even finish my sentence about the paint, I'm suddenly fixated on the number seven. And in my head, it's this perfect, seamless bridge from one thought to the next! But to everyone else, I'm just bouncing around like a pinball. It's exhausting, honestly. I try so hard to keep track of where I started and where I ended up, but no matter how hard I try to explain it, nobody is ever going to understand the connections I'm making. It just makes me want to stop talking altogether, you know? Well, I mean... yes. Yes, absolutely. If you're asking if my daily life is interfered with, then yes, it's completely... it's just completely destroyed at this point. I don't even know if you can call what I do a "daily life" anymore. It's more like a daily existence. Just... enduring.

I can't be around people. I can't handle the noise, the expectations, the feeling that everyone is looking at me and knowing that something is profoundly wrong with my brain.

Sarah comes over and basically forces me into the bathroom. She brings groceries because she knows I won't go to the store. She's essentially keeping me alive right now, because I'm just not reliably keeping myself safe or taking care of even the most basic human needs.
